You are skeptic #2. A WCAG/§4 audit of Heard's "provider-dashboard" screen produced this finding. Independently verify it by READING the cited code. Try to REFUTE it — default to real=false if the code already handles it, the claim is a stylistic nit, or it's not actually reachable by a user.

FILE: /Users/taha/Claude projects/TEWW apps/Therapy (Heard)/components/ui/DataTable.tsx
LOCATION: Line 68
RULE: 9
TITLE: Sort announcement uses hardcoded English instead of i18n
DETAIL: When a user clicks a sortable column header, the DataTable announces 'Sorted by {header}, {ascending|descending}' to screen readers. This message is hardcoded in English and not translatable via messages/en.json, violating Rule 9 (COPY via messages/en.json). Currently: `setAnnounce(\`Sorted by ${col.header}, ${dir === "asc" ? "ascending" : "descending"}\`)` This impacts any future internationalization and is inconsistent with the rest of the app which uses the t() i18n function for all user-facing copy.
SUGGESTION: Move the sort announcement to messages/en.json as a translatable string, e.g. 'provider.tableSort: "Sorted by {column}, {direction}"' and use the t() function to interpolate it with the column header and direction. Update the setAnnounce call to use t() instead of hardcoded text.

Return real=true ONLY if this is a genuine, actionable accessibility/polish gap that a fix would meaningfully improve.

This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

content.text: Now let me check how the `t()` function works and if there are any other examples of screen reader announcements in the codebase:
I see that DataTable.tsx does NOT import the `t()` function. Let me check how other components that do use `t()` import it:

Perfect! Now I can see the pattern. VoicePlayer imports `t` from `@/lib/i18n` and uses it in announcements (line 56 of VoicePlayer shows this). Let me verify the exact pattern used in VoicePlayer's announcement:
Now let me check if there is any existing pattern for table-related messages in the i18n file:
Let me also check where the DataTable component is actually being used to understand if sort announcements are actually user-facing:
Let me check one of the actual usages to see if sortable is even used:
Perfect! Now let me check one more table to see if sortable is actually used across the codebase:

Excellent! Now I have all the information I need. Let me summarize my findings:

## Analysis Summary

**Finding verified as REAL and ACTIONABLE:**

1. **Hardcoded English text confirmed**: Line 68 in DataTable.tsx contains:
   ```tsx
   setAnnounce(`Sorted by ${col.header}, ${dir === "asc" ? "ascending" : "descending"}`)
   ```

2. **The announcement is genuinely user-facing**: 
   - DataTable has `sortable: true` columns in actual production tables (SessionsTable.tsx lines 24-25, AdminActivityTables.tsx lines 91, 93, 99-100, 104)
   - The announcement goes into an `aria-live="polite"` region (line 168-170) which is announced to screen readers
   - This is not dead code—it's actively used in the provider dashboard and admin screens

3. **Violates the app's i18n pattern**:
   - Every other user-facing string uses `t()` function imported from `@/lib/i18n`
   - Examples: VoicePlayer.tsx line 5 and 58 uses `t("ui.announcePlaying", { name })`
   - All messages are stored in messages/en.json with dot-notation keys
   - DataTable does NOT import `t()` at all

4. **The suggestion is technically sound**:
   - Would add entries like `"provider.tableSort": "Sorted by {column}, {direction}"` to messages/en.json
   - Direction values ("ascending", "descending") could also be moved to i18n keys for consistency
   - The fix would make future i18n/l10n work seamless

**One minor caveat**: The app is currently English-only (no other language files visible), so this is not an immediate blocking issue. However, it's a legitimate accessibility and code consistency violation that violates Rule 9 (COPY via messages/en.json) and represents technical debt for future internationalization.

input.reason: The finding is valid. The sort announcement in DataTable.tsx line 68 uses hardcoded English text instead of i18n. It's production-facing code (used in SessionsTable, AdminActivityTables, etc.), announced to screen readers via aria-live, but does not use the app's standard t() i18n function. This violates the app's Rule 9 (COPY via messages/en.json) and creates inconsistency with the rest of the codebase. A fix would add translatable strings to messages/en.json and use the t() function, supporting future internationalization efforts.
